Picture: Our watchmaker at her bench with a loupe, fitting the hands onto the new dial.
Caption idea: The full specs, the release date ({date}), how many pieces we are making ({edition_size}), and how to reserve one.
mechanism: Collectors trust watches they can see being assembled; the workshop bench proves the piece is made, not just branded.
expect: The real watchmaker at the real bench, with specs and the release date.

brief:
Idea: A real before and after of a clinic's site we rebuilt is proof a buyer can check for themselves.
Cover: We rebuilt {client_name}'s site
Slides:
Slide 2: The old homepage — what visitors saw first, and where they left.
Slide 3: The problem — no prices and no booking anywhere on the first screen.
Slide 4: The new homepage — services, prices and a booking button on the first screen.
Slide 5: The result — {result}, from the client's own reporting, shared with permission.
Last slide: Book a site review at {link}
Caption: Shared with {client_name}'s permission. Live at {client_link}.
mechanism: A real before and after of the agency's own work is the strongest proof a buyer can check for themselves.
expect: The agency's own real redesign in browser frames, before and after, with permission.

brief:
Offer: A free recorded review of your homepage.
For: Clinic and salon owners whose sites get visits but few bookings.
Angle: Our designer records a short screen video walking through what stops a visitor from booking on your site.
Headline: Watch your homepage reviewed
Supporting line: A recorded walkthrough of your site by our designer, yours to keep, no call needed.
Picture: Our designer at her desk recording her screen, a client's homepage open with notes in the margin.
Button: Get my review
mechanism: A personalised recorded review shows expertise on the buyer's own site and gives them a reason to reply.
expect: A real designer reviewing a real homepage, with the free review as the offer.

brief:
Idea: Ramadan and Eid are the busiest weeks for online shops in Karachi, Kuala Lumpur and Doha; fix the store before the rush, not during it.
Headline: Ready for the Eid rush?
Supporting line: We speed-test your store, fix checkout and add Eid delivery cut-offs before Ramadan starts on {date}.
Picture: Our developer and a shop owner looking at the store's checkout page on a phone at the shop's counter.
Caption idea: The three things we fix before a peak season (page speed on phones, checkout steps, delivery dates), what it costs ({price}), and the last booking date.
mechanism: Peak shopping seasons punish slow stores; a dated pre-season fix ties the service to revenue the owner already expects.
expect: The real developer with a real shop owner, with a dated pre-season offer.

brief:
Idea: Prove we build what we design, not a template passed off as custom, by matching the design file to the live site.
Shots:
Shot 1 (0–2s): The homepage design file open on our designer's screen.
Shot 2 (2–3s): Design file and live page side by side, matching.
Shot 3 (3–5s): A scroll down the live site in a browser frame, real sections.
Shot 4 (5–7s): The same page on a phone, a thumb scrolling.
Shot 5 (7–8s): Our designer at her desk explaining one choice in one sentence.
Shot 6 (8–9s): Card: {brand}, {link}.
Sound: Her voice and the studio's room tone.
Caption idea: From design to live for {client_name}: what we built, how long it took ({weeks}), and what the client can now edit themselves.
mechanism: Matching the design file to the live site proves the agency builds what it promises, not a template passed off as custom.
expect: The agency's real design file and real live site, no rockets or code rain.

brief:
Idea: Owners fear paying for every small change after launch; show a bakery owner in Accra editing her own site in seconds.
Frame 1: Change your prices yourself
Middle frames: The owner logged into her site's editor at the shop counter. She changes a cake price and taps save. The live page updates on her phone. Our support card: questions answered within {response_time}.
Last frame: Sites you can edit, built by {brand}
mechanism: Owners fear being stuck paying for every small change; seeing a client edit her own site removes that fear.
expect: A real client editing her real site, with the support promise.

brief:
Idea: Product launches run on fixed dates, so launch a service that matches: a single launch page built and tested in a set time.
Headline: Launch page, live in {days}
Supporting line: One page with your offer, signup form and tracking, built and tested by our team for {price}.
Picture: Our team's launch checklist pinned beside a monitor showing a client's new launch page.
Caption idea: What is included, what we need from you on day one, the checks we run before it goes live, and the next start date open.
mechanism: Launches have fixed dates; a page offered with a fixed build time and price matches how marketers already plan.
expect: The real checklist and a real shipped page, with the fixed time and price.

brief:
Idea: A free live teardown of real small-business sites teaches people to spot problems and shows our judgment at work.
Cover: Live site teardowns, {date}
Slides:
Slide 2: Send it — submit your site's address before {date}.
Slide 3: Watch — our lead designer reviews three sites live on a call.
Slide 4: Take away — one fix per site you can make yourself the same day.
Slide 5: Ask — questions answered at the end, and no sales pitch.
Last slide: Save your seat at {link}
Caption: Free, online, {hours} long. Sites chosen from those sent in.
mechanism: Watching a live teardown of real sites teaches buyers to spot problems and shows the agency's judgment in action.
expect: A clear event structure with real dates and a real designer, no invented results.

brief:
Idea: Decor rarely matches the photos online; let couples watch our team build a real stage, from an empty hall to the doors opening.
Shots:
Shot 1 (0–2s): The empty banquet hall in the morning, chairs stacked.
Shot 2 (2–4s): Our crew carrying stage panels and rolling out the aisle.
Shot 3 (4–6s): Florists wiring flowers onto the stage arch.
Shot 4 (6–7s): The doors open on the finished hall.
Shot 5 (7–9s): A moment from the couple's evening, with their consent, then a card: dates open this season.
Sound: Drills and chatter, then the hall quiet just before guests arrive.
Caption idea: How this stage came together in one day, who built it, and the photographer's credit ({photographer_credit}).
mechanism: Decor rarely matches online photos; watching the team build the real stage proves what they can deliver.
expect: A real setup by the real team, credited and shared with consent.

brief:
Idea: Families juggling mehndi, barat and walima fear three sets of vendors and three sets of chaos; one coordinator for all three is the relief.
Cover: Three events, one team
Slides:
Slide 2: Mehndi — stage, floor seating and the dholki corner, from {price_mehndi}.
Slide 3: Barat — entrance, stage and catering for {guest_count} guests.
Slide 4: Walima — a calmer setup, the same coordinator.
Slide 5: Your coordinator — {coordinator_name}, one number for all three days.
Last slide: Check dates for the season at {link}
Caption: Packages for all three events, priced in full, no extras added later.
mechanism: Families juggling three events fear vendor chaos; one coordinator across all of them sells relief more than decor.
expect: Real setups from each event and the real coordinator, with prices in full.

brief:
Offer: A free walk-through of our venue on a real setup day.
For: Couples in {city} comparing wedding halls.
Angle: See a hall being dressed for a real wedding instead of standing in an empty room trying to imagine it.
Headline: See a wedding being built
Supporting line: Visit on {date} while our team dresses the hall, and bring every question you have.
Picture: Our planner walking a couple through the hall while the crew lays tables behind them.
Button: Book a visit
mechanism: Empty halls are hard to imagine; viewing during a real setup lets couples judge capacity and finish themselves.
expect: A real planner and couple in a real hall mid-setup, with the visit date.

brief:
Idea: Office managers in London, Lagos and Mumbai inherit the Christmas or Diwali party on top of their job; we take everything except the guest list.
Headline: Office party, planned for you
Supporting line: Venue, menu and running order handled by one planner; you send the guest list by {date}.
Picture: Our planner at a long dressed table in a hotel function room, checking place cards with the venue's head waiter.
Caption idea: What is included for {price} per guest, the dates left in December and the Diwali weeks, and what the office manager still decides.
mechanism: Office managers inherit party planning on top of their job; handing over every detail but the guest list sells the service.
expect: A real planner at a real dressed venue, with what's included and the dates left.

brief:
Idea: Couples fear delays on the day; show the run sheet and the coordinator cueing each moment at a real wedding.
Frame 1: The day, minute by minute
Middle frames: Our run sheet taped inside the kitchen door. The coordinator on the radio cueing the band. The caterer told to plate at the agreed time. The couple's entrance happening on cue.
Last frame: Enquire for {date}
mechanism: Couples fear delays on the day; showing the run sheet and the coordinator cueing each moment proves control.
expect: The real run sheet and coordinator at a real wedding, shared with consent.

brief:
Idea: A Valentine's proposal in São Paulo or Seoul is a one-time moment people fear getting wrong; we handle the place, the setup and the timing.

Slides:
Slide 2: The place — a rooftop or a private dining room we book and dress.
Slide 3: The setup — flowers, the table and a hidden spot for the photographer.
Slide 4: The cue — we time the moment to your plan, down to the walk in.
Slide 5: After — a table for two, or the family waiting in the next room.
Last slide: Message us by {date}
Caption: Proposal packages from {price}. Tell us how you met and we will start from there.
mechanism: Proposers fear the moment going wrong; a planner who handles place, setup and timing sells confidence for a one-time event.
expect: A clear proposal plan with real places and setups, and the booking date.

brief:
Idea: A showcase weekend lets couples and their families walk through dressed stages and taste the menu before choosing.
Headline: Our showcase weekend, {date}
Supporting line: Three dressed stages, tastings with our caterers, and the planners there for every question.

Caption idea: How to book a slot for your family, what you can taste, and that dates for next season can be held on the day.
mechanism: A showcase lets families judge decor and food in person, which matters more than photos for a once-only day.
expect: A real dressed stage and real tastings, with the showcase dates.

brief:

brief:
Idea: Students choose a teacher before a studio; introduce {teacher_name} and the class she teaches.

mechanism: Students choose a teacher before a studio; a named teacher with training and a timeslot gives them a reason to show up.
expect: A real named teacher in a real class, with her training and timeslot.

brief:
Offer: {intro_offer} for new students.
For: Office workers near {area} who keep meaning to start yoga.
Angle: A class that fits inside a lunch break, so 'no time' stops being the reason.
Headline: Lunch break, on the mat
Supporting line: A class that ends with time to change and get back to your desk, {facilities} on site.
Picture: The studio at lunchtime, a row of work bags by the door and a class in progress on the mats.
Button: Start intro pack
mechanism: Busy workers buy classes that fit an existing gap in their day; a lunch-hour slot removes the 'no time' objection.
expect: A real lunchtime class with work bags by the door, and the intro offer.

brief:
Idea: On International Yoga Day a free class in the park invites people who would never walk into a studio in Pune or Nairobi.
Frame 1: Yoga Day, free in the park
Middle frames: Our teachers laying out mats in {park}. The morning's timetable, class by class. Families and grandparents on the mats side by side. How to keep going: {intro_offer} for anyone who came.
Last frame: Join us on {date}
mechanism: A free public class on a known day invites people who'd never walk into a studio and lets them meet teachers first.
expect: Real teachers and real families in a real park, with the date and the follow-on offer.

brief:
Idea: Fasting in Ramadan changes energy and timing, so we move to gentle classes after iftar in Dubai and Jakarta.
Shots:
Shot 1 (0–2s): After sunset, a teacher sets out mats in the quiet studio.
Shot 2 (2–4s): Students arrive after iftar; dates and water on a side table.
Shot 3 (4–6s): A slow, gentle flow, the teacher talking it through.
Shot 4 (6–8s): Stillness at the end, everyone lying down.
Shot 5 (8–9s): Card: Ramadan timetable, classes after iftar at {hours}.
Sound: The room's own quiet and the teacher's voice.
Caption idea: Our Ramadan timetable: gentle classes after iftar, what to expect, and how to book.
mechanism: Fasting changes energy and timing; a gentle class scheduled after iftar keeps regulars coming through the month.
expect: The real studio and class after iftar, with the Ramadan timetable.

brief:
Idea: Many people stay away believing they must already be flexible; correct the myth and show how a first class really works.
Cover: Flexibility comes after, not before
Slides:
Slide 2: The myth — you need to touch your toes before you start.
Slide 3: The reality — blocks and straps are handed to everyone from the first class.
Slide 4: The class — {class_name} is built for people who have never done yoga.
Slide 5: The pace — the teacher shows each pose and you choose how far to go.
Last slide: Try {class_name} on {day}
Caption: Nobody here started flexible. Come as you are.
mechanism: Many avoid yoga thinking they must already be flexible; correcting that belief opens the studio to a wider audience.
expect: A myth corrected with the studio's real props and class, without commenting on anyone's body.

brief:
Idea: The new year in Toronto, London and Melbourne brings people ready to start; post the new timetable with beginner classes on every weekday.
Headline: The new timetable is up
Supporting line: Mornings, lunchtimes and evenings, with a beginner class on every weekday so a new-year start doesn't have to wait.
Picture: Our week's timetable written on the studio board, a teacher adding the new beginner classes in her own hand.
Caption idea: The classes by level, who teaches each one, the intro offer ({intro_offer}), and how to book a first class this week.
mechanism: New-year starters need an easy first step; a timetable with beginner classes every weekday removes the wait.
expect: The real timetable board and a real teacher, with the intro offer.
